what: the independent reading of every shared sentence, the round that fixed the false ones and the unsound matching, its independent check, and the survey of the twenty runtimes

digest.part: The independent reading of every shared sentence (s3b, three reviewers, 297 sentences), brief 6 that set the fix round, the tools round (sound masking and sentence identity, re-key), the shared round (false sentences fixed once, frozen at v33s), its independent check (ok: false), and the survey of the twenty runtimes (12 questions, one reader's claim per line). All six records were present and read in full; brief.md was read for H1-H5.

rounds.purpose: Read every distinct shared sentence once against the runtimes. Until then most shared sentences had been accepted by pattern rules and never read (brief6).
rounds.who: Three independent reviewers, parts A (tutorial 71 + rootquick 19 = 90), B (reference ids 0-7, 100) and C (reference ids 8-f, 107). All three say they read; none compiled or ran an example. B ran one strict-mode JS one-liner; A and C ran only node, grep and awk scripts over stored output.
rounds.produced: 297 verdicts. A: 72 ok, 4 false, 14 awkward. B: 85 ok, 7 false, 8 awkward. C: 91 ok, 3 false, 13 awkward. Merged (brief6): 248 ok, 35 awkward, 14 false. The 14 false ids are six distinct sentences. They also produced fix entries, per-language defects, and two findings that the matching itself is unsound: the mask hides shared words, and one template is counted as many sentences.
rounds.changed: Brief 6 opened a fix round with a new rule: a sentence is reviewed once only if the tools can tell what the same sentence is; one template gives one verdict; a token is masked only where a language or the model supplied it; a false sentence is fixed once in shared code and must be true of all twenty runtimes; a changed sentence has no verdict until someone other than its author reads it.

rounds.purpose: Turn the review into a fix round with three roles.
rounds.who: The workflow brief. Roles: tools (P/sfix/tools), shared (P/sfix/sdkgen, after tools), verify (independent reader and adversary).
rounds.produced: The work list: five false-sentence topics, the 35 awkward ids, the per-language defects, and the two matching flaws.
rounds.changed: Set the base: v3.2 frozen (tag v32-frozen); nine languages (ts go py c zig clojure rust elixir rb) ported; perl, swift, ocaml and lua being ported in parallel; seven to follow.

rounds.purpose: Make sentence identity and masking sound, re-key every record keyed by a class or sentence id, carry the verdicts over, and close three holes in the one command.
rounds.who: One tools engineer. No independent check inside this record; the verify round checked it.
rounds.produced: Tools at 7d5dab2 (later 740dc90 after the shared round). Learned model slots per template across 21 variations with the language under review left out; a new sentence identity (ident.js); a bold-lead split; rekey.js; buildfresh.js (stale build); handstale.js (stale hand records); sharewords.js on the new identity. The 297 old ids map to 227, all with a verdict (ok 194, awkward 26, false 7). Self-test 203 controls, 0 failed, 1 moved.
rounds.changed: Nine one commands pass after the re-key. 10 classes were recorded by hand by the tools engineer (go 3 conflicts and 2 split parts, rb 5 false-verdict classes). The tools engineer predicted 5 open classes for each port, which the verify round later measured as 16 for lua.

rounds.purpose: Check each false sentence against the runtimes (run where possible), fix each once in shared code, decide the awkward ones, fix the per-language defects in providers, re-review the nine languages with the new tools, freeze.
rounds.who: One engineer. Ran probes in ts, py and go; read the other runtimes and relied on the survey for questions 9 to 11.
rounds.produced: sdkgen tagged v33s at e84d3525 (9 commits on v32-frozen 3d58cb46); tools at 740dc90. One runtime fix (b09502f1, ts and js makeFeature fallback, with a test). All six false sentences fixed once in shared code. 20 awkward decisions (applied, improved or left). 10 per-language defect fixes. Two breaking interface changes (read truth flag, required ref.facts.testMock) and three additive ones. 376 classes reopened, 361 hand records added, 16 stale reasons rewritten. 41 changed or new sentences left without a verdict, for an independent reader.
rounds.changed: H1 breaking-change count now about 22 to 24 against a line of about 10. The eleven unported languages' pages stayed byte-identical (418 files). The four ports in progress must declare testMock 'generated' and, for swift and ocaml, a truth read.

rounds.purpose: Independently read every changed sentence and attack the new matching.
rounds.who: One independent verifier, on copies of sfix/sdkgen (v33s), sfix/tools (740dc90) and ports/lua. Re-ran the freeze checks, the probes (ts, py, go, including an own go probe), a revert of the runtime fix, 26 attacks in both modes, re-keys, the lua port procedure and the stale checks.
rounds.produced: ok: False. Verdicts on the 41: 39 ok, 2 awkward, 0 false. Every freeze number reproduced. Six required failures: the match form accepts any own fact anywhere (4 wrong-prose changes accepted automatically); numbers and the a/an article are masked; dropping go's or c's branch sentence leaves no trace; buildfresh misses model files; handstale accepts OLD-page quotes; the lua port procedure run literally fails with 16 open classes, not 5.
rounds.changed: Ten required fixes listed (tools ident.js/classify.js, controls, buildfresh, handstale, the port procedure, two wordings in ReadmeRef.ts, the unported README test-mode sections, commit trailers, re-reading 3 carried awkward verdicts). The round is not accepted as ready.

rounds.round: s3c survey of the twenty runtimes (short form)
rounds.purpose: Answer twelve questions about runtime behaviour for all 20 bundled languages, so sentences can be checked against every runtime rather than the nine ported ones.
rounds.who: Readers of the runtime source; 'every line is one reader's claim'. Each answer is marked 'read and certain' or 'read and inferred'; nothing in the short form says it was run. Full answers with file, line and quote are in P/results/s3c-survey.md (not in my records).
rounds.produced: One line per runtime for: accessor and cache, getters copy or live, stream signal, cancelling an operation, when a stream's operation runs, after remove, what each thing is called on, fields or calls, direct's result in four cases, the test constructor without the test feature, ctrl.explain, what a standalone program must import.

disagreements.a: Each port should expect 5 open classes (the false-verdict sentences) after the re-key and one command.
disagreements.b: The lua port procedure run literally fails with 16 open classes (tutorial 6, reference 10), because nothing moves the port onto v33s; the shared engineer also says the 5 expected classes no longer exist.
disagreements.stands: b: 16 open, measured; the procedure needs a step that rebases the port on v33s.

disagreements.a: Match form: a position is masked only if its text is one of the language's own declared facts and no other language prints it as plain text; one template gives one id, and the masking is sound against a port or regression.
disagreements.b: The match form accepts any own fact at any position: four wrong-prose changes were accepted automatically in both modes; numbers and the a/an article are also masked.

disagreements.a: Retargeting sentence-removed-go to drop go's 'A key is read as ...' sentence keeps the control's intent.
disagreements.b: The control should have kept its v3.2 intent (drop go's branch sentence) and been recorded as moved: dropping go's or c's branch sentence from every variation leaves no trace even in the reviewed mode.

disagreements.a: buildfresh closes the hole that the one command passed on an old build.
disagreements.b: buildfresh does not compare ts/project/.sdk/model/** with its staged copy: a model edit without a build passes (787 files would differ once staged).

disagreements.a: handstale closes the hole of a hand record that stays decided after its quoted text changed.
disagreements.b: handstale accepts a quotation found on any OLD page, so a reason quoting text that left NEW and the source stays green.

disagreements.a: Proposed fix for the ctrl example: `{ explain: {} }`, a map the call fills.
disagreements.b: Also false: direct() records nothing in explain, and php ignores an empty array; the example was removed ('Control options.').
disagreements.b_source: s3c-sfix-shared.txt false_sentences[2]; confirmed in s3c-sfix-verify.txt false_checks[2]

disagreements.a: The no-test test-client sentences are false for ts and true for the other runtimes (go, c, py, rust fall back to the base feature).
disagreements.b: zig and clojure keep the real mock without the test feature, so 'no mock transport' is false for them too; it became the declared fact testMock.
disagreements.b_source: s3c-sfix-shared.txt false_sentences[3]; s3c-sfix-verify.txt false_checks[3]; survey question 10

disagreements.b: False where the entity holds a stored match (ts list passes this._match); only 'The match is optional.' kept.

findings.finding: Reading every shared sentence once found real errors: of 297 distinct sentences, 14 ids (six distinct sentences) were false and 35 awkward. One false sentence (the client reads the API key from the environment) was introduced by the shared code itself and accepted by eight rule records nobody read; two others were false on main's old pages already.

Each false sentence was checked by running ts, py and (for two topics) go SDKs, then fixed once in shared code; an independent verifier re-ran all six and agreed. The eleven unported languages' pages did not change (418 files byte-identical).

Writing a sentence once forces it to be true of all twenty runtimes, which surfaced differences nobody had listed: zig and clojure keep the mock without the test feature, ts and js test() threw, ts throws on explain true. The first became a declared fact (testMock), the second a runtime fix with a test.

H1's interface threshold is crossed: the fix round added two breaking changes (a truth flag on the read printer, a required testMock fact), for about 22 to 24 breaking changes since the first four languages against a line of about 10. Neither came from a newly ported language.

By source, per-language prose stays well under H1's 15% line in the nine ported languages (highest go 7.4%). By page, only 9 of 77 sentences printed by one language are a runtime's own fact; 50 are shared code that one condition selects.

The v3.2 matching was unsound: shared words were masked as model names, and one template counted as many sentences (178 of 297 named one language). The tools round fixed both kinds of split (297 ids to 227) and passed 5 new masking controls that v3.2 failed in 6 of 10 runs.

The independent check failed the round (ok: false). The v3.3 match form still accepts wrong prose automatically when a language's own fact of another kind stands in the slot: four such attacks were accepted in both modes. Wrong numbers and a wrong article before a model name leave no trace, and dropping go's or c's branch sentence from every variation is not detected even in the reviewed mode.

Two of the tools' new safety checks have holes. The stale-build check misses model files: an unstaged model edit is reported current, though 787 output files would differ. The stale-record check accepts quotations found only on OLD pages.

Changing a few shared sentences is expensive under the current tools. It reopened 376 classes and needed 361 new hand records. The heading change alone re-paired about 100 classes per language, and 40 self-test controls failed because their text had changed.

The documented procedure for moving an in-progress port onto the new tools does not reach a passing one command. On lua it left 16 open classes against the 5 predicted, because no step rebases the port on v33s.

Example lanes pass at v33s. The lanes were ts README 16/16, go 12/12, py 12/12, c 6/6, rust 6/6, rb 49/49 and zig 6/6. No lane compiles the changed blocks or the new self-contained Action Call cells (go, c, zig, elixir), so H4 holds only for what the lanes cover.

The survey of all 20 runtimes is read, not run, and each line is one reader's claim. It shows where a shared sentence can be one sentence and where a declared fact is needed. direct()'s result and explain handling are the same in all 20. Stream signals, cancellation, when a stream's operation runs, accessor caching and live-or-copy getters differ by runtime.

Several fix-round decisions were made by one engineer and never re-read by another. These are 10 hand-decided classes, mechanically carried mixed and fromSplit verdicts, and re-paired classes reusing v3.2 decisions. Verdicts for the runtimes without a toolchain rest on reading.
